title: Rerank surge mitigation: adaptive regional warm pools, KV prefetch, and circuit throttling
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Background: Production reranker endpoints observe large tail-latency spikes during unexpected traffic surges and cross-region failovers. Root causes identified in runtime traces: cold KV-cache misses, expensive kernel selection during on-demand warmup, and uncoordinated fanout to heavyweight ranking replicas. Goal: implement a multi-pronged surge mitigation strategy that reduces tail latency and failure rate during 3-5x short-duration QPS spikes while preserving ranking quality.
acceptance_criteria: During synthetic 5x QPS spike test, p95 latency for rerank endpoint does not exceed 1.8x baseline and p99 does not exceed 3x baseline
Error rate (5xx) for rerank endpoints remains below 0.2% during spike tests
Warm pool reduces cold-start KV miss rate by 60% on first request after idle period
Circuit throttling prevents cascading failures: when regional capacity crosses threshold, requests are degraded to cached-local variant with documented quality delta
Rollout can be toggled per-region and fully rolled back within 5 minutes via console flags
design_notes: High-level approach: 1) Regional adaptive warm pools: maintain a small set of standby worker processes with warmed model weights and primed KV caches per region. Pool size computed from recent tail traffic percentile and scaled with a fast-path autoscaler. 2) KV prefetch on admission: when a request is enqueued, issue low-priority KV prefetch for top-k candidates derived from fast approximate embedding match; attach prefetch token to request context so subsequent rerank invocation reuses cache. 3) Hybrid circuit throttling: a soft QoS layer reduces concurrency via admission control and a hard circuit breaker trips to route new requests to read-only cached replica variants (cached-ranking or approximate reranker) when regional SLOs are violated. 4) Routing policy: region-aware fanout with dynamic weights; prefer local warm pool, fallback to nearest healthy region, then cached-local variant. Track provenance for quality monitoring.
implementation_steps: Prototype warm pool manager in runtime agent: lifecycle APIs (warm, drain, health-check)
Add KV prefetch hook in admission controller: gather top-k keys from embedding-indexer and issue async prefetch
Implement soft admission QoS token bucket with backlog-aware decrement and priority lanes
Add a hard circuit breaker state machine tied to regional SLOs and recent error/latency windows
Enhance routing layer to support multi-tier fallback: warm pool -> local scaled cluster -> remote region -> cached replica
Integrate rollout flags into console with per-region controls and canary percentage
Build end-to-end test harness (chaos + spike driver) and add dashboard panels for warm-pool occupancy, prefetch hit rate, circuit state
test_plan: Unit tests for warm pool lifecycle, prefetch hook, and circuit state transitions
Integration test in staging: simulate 5x QPS surge for 10 minutes with mixed query distributions and assert acceptance criteria
Chaos scenarios: kill warm pool nodes, saturate KV backend, induce cross-region latency and validate fallback correctness
A/B evaluation: run 10% traffic with feature on and compare NDCG@10 against baseline and monitor quality regression alerts
Load test with embedding-heavy queries to verify prefetch effectiveness and measure end-to-end cost delta
rollback_plan: Feature flags at routing and runtime level allow immediate global disable. If p95 or error rates exceed thresholds during rollout, flip per-region flag to off, which drains warm pools and restores previous routing; ops playbook to reopen traffic gradually after investigation.
notes_for_reviewers: Key trade-offs: warm pools reduce cold-start latency but increase baseline resource footprint; prefetch risks loading irrelevant keys and increasing KV load—we will throttle prefetch rate based on observed hit rate. Need help from runtime and infra teams to size warm pools conservatively for initial rollout. Ask: review circuit thresholds and fallback quality deltas before implementation.
